integrity.containment_basis: For diagonal \(A\) and \(B\), the projective principal-minor map is the standard Segre monomial map, hence every tensor-coordinate point lies in the variety.
integrity.first_public_date_basis: Borodin--Rains arXiv:math-ph/0409059 was first submitted on 2004-09-21 and already defines the projective determinantal-point variety later identified with the projective principal-minor variety.
integrity.fixed_locus_basis: Powers-of-two diagonal weights separate all tensor-coordinate weights, so the ambient projective fixed locus consists exactly of \(2^n\) coordinate points.
integrity.invariance_basis: Both archival sources record invariance under the natural \(\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb C)^n\) action.
integrity.localization_basis: Compactly supported Euler characteristic localizes to the fixed locus for algebraic \(\mathbb C^*\)-actions, and projectivity identifies it with ordinary Euler characteristic.
integrity.object_basis: Lin--Sturmfels define the projective principal-minor map and state that its image is a closed cone; Borodin--Rains define the same determinantal-point variety and Lin--Sturmfels explicitly identify the overlap.
integrity.primary_slot_basis: Lin--Sturmfels arXiv:0812.0601 is an algebraic-geometry source and lists MSC 14M12 first.

scientific_limitations: Only ordinary topological Euler characteristic of the projective variety and compactly supported Euler characteristic of its complement are computed.
No claim is made about Betti numbers, Hodge numbers, motives, intersection cohomology, singularities, degree, or defining equations.
The argument is short once the known group invariance and diagonal Segre locus are combined, so an unindexed or folklore observation remains possible.
title: The projective principal-minor variety has ambient Euler characteristic
